text:
Aisha: Opening a quick thread about improving postmortem follow-ups. We keep seeing stale remediation tickets. Idea: a lightweight "follow-up runner" that nudges owners and escalates when needed.
Kenji: Strong yes. Can we keep it minimal so it doesn't add noise?
Aisha: Totally. Plan: weekly digest + direct pings only for overdue items. Suggest SLAs: P1 remediations 14 days, P2 30 days.
Marta: Add an owner confirmation step: when an action is created, owner must ack within 48h or it gets flagged for reassignment.
Liam: Also surface "recurrence matches" from past PMs so teams know if this is a repeat failure mode.
Kenji: Comms cadence idea: weekly summary in #incidents (public) with counts and links; DMs to owners for specifics. Escalations go to oncall lead and manager.
Aisha: Three deliverables: 1) standardized timeline template in PM docs, 2) follow-up runner service (cron + bot), 3) escalation policy + IC rotation reminders.
IncidentBot: Registered: follow-up-runner cron (Mon 09:00 UTC)  will DM owners for overdue items.
Marta: Draft timeline snippet I'll add to the PM template:

```
postmortem_timeline:
  - name: "RCA published"
    target_days: "2"
    owner: "<name>"
  - name: "Actions assigned"
    target_days: "5"
    owner: "<name>"
  - name: "Remediation review"
    target_days: "14"
    owner: "<name>"
  - name: "Verification & close"
    target_days: "30"
    owner: "<name>"
  - related_incidents: []
  - recurrence_risk: "low|medium|high"
```

Kenji: Nice. If the template includes related_incidents links the runner can query and surface matches.
Liam: Metrics request: track percent on-time, mean time to remediate, number of reassignments. Put a small metric tag in runner messages.
Marta: Implementation notes: simple lambda that reads tracker (Confluence sheet), filters open actions, computes overdue by SLA, groups by owner, posts DM + a single summary thread in #postmortem-followups. DM text example: "You have 2 overdue items from PM #4321: <link>. Please update by Tue 5 May or reply with new ETA."
Aisha: For IC rotation: publish a 6-week roster doc and have the runner remind the next IC 24h before. Also auto-post the current IC in #oncall each week.
Kenji: Ownership change flow: owner can reply "reassign @person" in the DM and bot will create a reassignment request comment on the PM doc and ping the new owner. Manual approval optional.
Liam: I'll draft the Console metric spec so product can visualize trends. This will help prioritize which recurring issues need deeper investment.
Marta: I'll prototype the runner and share a sample message format. Want to test with three historical PMs to validate recurrence detection.
Kenji: I'll prepare a few PM examples and a short list of edge cases (incidents with multiple owners, cross-team items).
Aisha: Sounds good. Next step: Marta + Kenji to ship an MVP runner + template by EOD Friday; Aisha will write escalation policy; Liam owns metrics.
Marta: I'll open a small repo and a Confluence test sheet and ping for review.
IncidentBot: Action created: "MVP follow-up-runner" assigned to Marta, Kenji, due 7 days from now.
Aisha: Thanks team. If we like the pilot we can roll it org-wide. :thumbsup:
